candidate.title: Webhook secret header lookup uses raw env header name, breaking auth due to lowercased req.headers keys
reports: webhook handler uses process.env.calcomwebhookheadername raw for header lookup; since node lowercases headers, any uppercase in the env value makes auth always fail with 403

process.env.calcomwebhookheadername is used as-is for header lookup in app-credential.ts; node lowercases incoming header names, so an env value with uppercase letters causes every request to be rejected with 403; value should be normalized with .tolowercase()

[low/bug] the header name from calcomwebhookheadername is used without .tolowercase() even though node lowercases incoming header keys (a mixed-case value silently rejects valid secrets), and req.headers[...] may be string[], making the strict comparison always fail.

req.headers[...] in app-credential.ts can be string | string[] | undefined with no normalization or type narrowing — a repeated header yields an array that never equals the secret, and a non-lowercase calcomwebhookheadername will never match next.js's lowercased header map

webhook secret verification weaknesses: the secret is compared with plain !== (non-constant-time, minor timing side channel), and req.headers[process.env.calcomwebhookheadername] is looked up without lowercasing the env value — node lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case calcomwebhookheadername silently 403s every valid webhook (app-credential.ts:24-27)

[advisory] the configured header name is used as-is to index req.headers, but node lowercases all incoming header names, so an env value like 'calcom-webhook-secret' looks up a key that never exists. a self-hoster setting the header name in conventional casing gets a 403 'invalid webhook secret' on every request despite a correct secret, with the only hint being a comment in .env.example.
candidate.example: if calcomwebhookheadername is set with uppercase characters, node's lowercased incoming headers will never match — fail-closed but a configuration footgun

fix_scope: minimal fix for the demonstrated instance only

sibling_instances.note: other instances of this class are unverified siblings; fix.patch does not address them

claim_restated: The webhook handler incorrectly indexes req.headers using the raw (possibly mixed-case) env header name and does not normalize string[] header values, causing valid webhook secrets to be rejected with 403.
expected_failure: Webhook auth should lowercase the env-configured header name (Node lowercases req.headers keys) and normalize string[] header values

multi_defect.explanation: Most findings share the lowercasing mismatch, but findings 1/2 add duplicate-header array handling, finding 6 adds an undefined-config auth bypass, and finding 4 adds timing-safe comparison as separate defects.
multi_defect.status: the promoted verdict verifies ONE of these defects; the other(s) are unverified extras
